about.title: Shasta Lake Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Shasta Lake is a small city, but its workers face real risks — whether on a delivery route along Cascade Boulevard, at a facility near Wonderland Boulevard, or on a job that has them driving through town during the Tuesday evening rush. When a workplace injury happens, California law usually routes your claim through workers' compensation, regardless of who was at fault. But that's not always the full picture. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim against that third party. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured workers in Shasta Lake with an independent attorney who can look at both angles of your situation. There's no cost to find out where you stand, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless your claim results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Shasta Lake Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Look Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — may owe you separately. We help connect you with an attorney who checks for that possibility.

items.title: We Know the Reporting Clock Matters
items.desc: California requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate your claim, so timing matters from day one.

items.title: Retaliation Protection Is on Your Side
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. An attorney can help you understand your protections if you feel pressured.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site near Shasta Dam Boulevard — does workers' comp cover everything?
items.answer: Workers' comp is usually your primary path against your employer, no matter who was at fault. But if a property owner, contractor, or equipment supplier at that site contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate third-party claim. An independent attorney can review the specifics of your job site incident to see if that applies.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury or file a claim?
items.answer: You generally need to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. If a third party is involved, that separate claim typically carries a 2-year deadline in California. Acting sooner rather than later helps preserve your options.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting a work injury in Shasta Lake?
items.answer: No — retaliation against an employee for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim is illegal under California law. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an attorney can help you understand what steps to take next.
